questions.question: Which range is IPv6 global unicast (public)?

correct.explanation: 2000::/3 is the IPv6 global unicast range — publicly routable addresses.

incorrect.explanation: FE80::/10 is link-local — not globally routable public unicast.
incorrect.whatItDoes: FE80::/10 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (global unicast): 2000::/3 matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — FE80::/10 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: FC00::/7 is unique local (ULA) — private-like, not global public unicast.
incorrect.whatItDoes: FC00::/7 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (global unicast): 2000::/3 matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — FC00::/7 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: FF00::/8 is multicast — not unicast public addressing.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting multicast range for unicast question
incorrect.whatItDoes: FF00::/8 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (global unicast): 2000::/3 matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — FF00::/8 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

answerReview.examTip: Global unicast = 2000::/3. Link-local = FE80::/10. ULA = FC00::/7.

questions.question: What does an IPv6 link-local address begin with?

correct.explanation: IPv6 link-local addresses begin with FE80::/10.

incorrect.explanation: FF02::/16 is multicast — not link-local unicast.
incorrect.whatItDoes: FF02 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for link-local.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "link-local", FE80 satisfies what this question tests — FF02 does not.

incorrect.explanation: 2001::/32 is global unicast space.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 2001 gives a numeric value (timer, prefix, or rate) that may not match the fact tested in link-local.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "link-local", FE80 satisfies what this question tests — 2001 does not.

incorrect.explanation: FD00::/8 is unique local (ULA) — not FE80 link-local.
incorrect.whatItDoes: FD00 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for link-local.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "link-local", FE80 satisfies what this question tests — FD00 does not.

questions.question: Which is the IPv6 “private” (RFC1918-like) range commonly used?
questions.explanation: Unique Local is FC00::/7, used in practice as FD00::/8.

correct.explanation: FD00::/8 is IPv6 unique local (RFC 4193) — analogous to private IPv4.

incorrect.explanation: 2000::/3 is global unicast allocation.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 2000::/3 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (unique local): FD00::/8 matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — 2000::/3 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: FE80::/10 is link-local — not site-private ULA.
incorrect.whatItDoes: FE80::/10 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (unique local): FD00::/8 matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — FE80::/10 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: FF00::/8 is multicast.
incorrect.whatItDoes: FF00::/8 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (unique local): FD00::/8 matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — FF00::/8 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

questions.question: Which multicast address reaches all routers on a link?
questions.explanation: FF02::2 = all routers; FF02::1 = all nodes.

correct.explanation: FF02::2 is all-routers on the local link multicast group.

incorrect.explanation: FF02::1 is all-nodes — every host, not routers only.
incorrect.whatItDoes: FF02::1 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for multicast.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "multicast", FF02::2 satisfies what this question tests — FF02::1 does not.

incorrect.explanation: FF02::5 is OSPFv3 — not generic all-routers.
incorrect.whatItDoes: FF02::5 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for multicast.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "multicast", FF02::2 satisfies what this question tests — FF02::5 does not.

incorrect.explanation: 224.0.0.2 is IPv4 multicast — question is IPv6.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 224.0.0.2 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for multicast.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "multicast", FF02::2 satisfies what this question tests — 224.0.0.2 does not.

questions.question: True or False: IPv6 uses a broadcast address like IPv4.
questions.explanation: False — IPv6 has no broadcast; multicast (FF00::/8) replaces it.

correct.explanation: False — IPv6 uses multicast instead of broadcast; there is no IPv6 broadcast address.

incorrect.explanation: IPv6 eliminated broadcast — uses solicited-node and other multicast groups.
incorrect.whatItDoes: True states the opposite of the tested fact about no broadcast.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "no broadcast", False satisfies what this question tests — True does not.

questions.question: The same IPv6 address is configured on several servers and traffic goes to the nearest. What type is this?
questions.explanation: Anycast = one address on multiple devices, delivered to the nearest.

correct.explanation: Same address on multiple nodes with nearest delivery is anycast.

incorrect.explanation: Multicast is one-to-many — anycast is one-to-nearest of identical addresses.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Multicast gives a broadcast or multicast MAC pattern that may not be the all-ones form tested here.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "Anycast = one address on multiple devices, delivered to the nearest", Anycast satisfies what this question tests — Multicast does not.

incorrect.explanation: Link-local is FE80::/10 scope — not anycast semantics.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Link-local states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (Anycast = one address on multiple devices, delivered to the nearest): Anycast matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — Link-local breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: IPv6 has no broadcast.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Broadcast describes flooding the frame to multiple ports in the VLAN.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "Anycast = one address on multiple devices, delivered to the nearest", Anycast satisfies what this question tests — Broadcast does not.

questions.question: Where can a link-local (FE80::) address be used?
questions.explanation: Link-local is never routed off the local link.

correct.explanation: Link-local FE80:: addresses are valid only on the local link — not routable remotely.

incorrect.explanation: FE80 is not Internet-routable.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Across the internet points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for link-local scope.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "link-local scope", Only on the local link satisfies what this question tests — Across the internet does not.

incorrect.explanation: All IPv6 hosts use link-local — not router-only.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Only by routers points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for link-local scope.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "link-local scope", Only on the local link satisfies what this question tests — Only by routers does not.

incorrect.explanation: Link-local does not require NAT66.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Only with NAT points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for link-local scope.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "link-local scope", Only on the local link satisfies what this question tests — Only with NAT does not.

questions.question: Which multicast group does every IPv6 host join?
questions.explanation: All IPv6 hosts join FF02::1, the all-nodes group.

correct.explanation: Every IPv6 node joins FF02::1 (all-nodes link-local multicast).

incorrect.explanation: FF02::2 is all-routers — hosts join all-nodes too.
incorrect.whatItDoes: FF02::2 (all routers) points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for all nodes.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "all nodes", FF02::1 (all nodes) satisfies what this question tests — FF02::2 (all routers) does not.

incorrect.explanation: FE80::1 is not the all-nodes multicast group.
incorrect.whatItDoes: FE80::1 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (all nodes): FF02::1 (all nodes) matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — FE80::1 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: 2000::/3 is global unicast — not mandatory multicast membership.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 2000::1 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for all nodes.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "all nodes", FF02::1 (all nodes) satisfies what this question tests — 2000::1 does not.
